old_title: Ukraine war latest: Trump celebrates release of US prisoner in Russia
new_title: Ukraine live: Attack on Kyiv shows talks with Putin make no difference, says Zelensky

Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social to celebrate Vladimir Putin's decision to release Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen who was formally designated as wrongfully detained in Russia for four years.
Mr Hubbard's release came after Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian president Vladimir Putin on ending the Ukraine war.
Witkoff has come straight from Norway, where he met with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky in a bid to stabilise worsening relations between Kyiv and Washington.
In televised remarks at the beginning of his meeting with Putin, Witkoff said his goal was to discuss the resumption of trilateral talks involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
He said a resumption of talks would allow technical teams to discuss the next steps toward a peace settlement.
Meanwhile, a Wall Street Journal report said it was Elon Musk who ordered the slowdown of Ukraine's access to his military-grade Starlink satellite internet, which is critical for Kyiv's attack and defence drone capabilities. Musk has previously claimed such decisions are down to the military and the president.
South Korea to recall some of its diplomats from Kyiv
South Korea will withdraw some of its diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid worsening relations between Seoul and Kyiv over the disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs), Yonhap news agency reported, citing Seoul's foreign ministry.
"This measure was taken because we judged it necessary to facilitate an amicable resolution of the issue and restore trust between the two countries," foreign ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon said, according to Yonhap.
The move follows South Korea's decision to recall its ambassador to Ukraine on 8 October after Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky publicly disclosed the transfer of the two prisoners to South Korea during his speech at the UN General Assembly on 23 September.
Seoul claims the announcement violated a confidentiality agreement between the two countries.
Trump hails Putin for releasing US citizen Stephen Hubbard
Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social to celebrate Vladimir Putin's decision to release Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen who was formally designated as wrongfully detained in Russia for four years.
"Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family. The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return - an unprecedented situation for Russia," the post read.
Hubbard's release comes after a number of US concessions towards Russia in recent weeks, including a deal signed by Trump to obtain diesel from Moscow.
Nonetheless, Trump claimed that "there was no 'swap' necessary for this release".
"Welcome home Stephen, it's great to have you back," the statement quoted Trump as saying.
Trump's envoy says he hopes to restart three-way talks with Russia and Ukraine
In televised remarks at the beginning of his meeting with Vladimir Putin, Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff said his goal was to discuss the resumption of trilateral talks involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
He said a resumption of talks would allow technical teams to discuss the next steps toward a peace settlement.
Witkoff and Putin met at St Petersburg's Constantine Palace, with Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev and Putin's foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov also at the table. Witkoff said Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner would join the discussion via a video link.
Witkoff said he would inform Putin about Tuesday's talks in Oslo, which he described as "productive," adding that "there is some degree of momentum."
He thanked Putin for lifting Russia's ban on diesel exports, which angered some US lawmakers, adding that it would help reduce prices for US farmers and truckers.
Putin thanked Trump and Witkoff for their efforts to end the war and said he was ready to discuss restoring US-Russian economic ties.
Putin was also due to meet later on Wednesday with Chinese premier Li Qiang, who is in St Petersburg meeting with other Russian top officials, the Kremlin said.
'I lay in a pool of blood after being shot at point blank range while undercover in Northern Ireland'
A former member of one of the British Army's most secret surveillance units has, for the first time, told the dramatic story of his role in an undercover operation that ended with him being shot through the stomach, his partner mortally wounded, and a wanted IRA gunman fleeing injured into the night.
The veteran, known only as Blue*, recounted how events unfolded in episode five of SAS: The Shadow War.
He was just 22 and serving with 14 Intelligence Company - the clandestine unit known simply as "the Det" - when he and another soldier set up a covert observation post beside a farm in South Derry on St Patrick's Day, 17 March 1978.
Putin says he and Trump could meet in China
Russian president Vladimir Putin proposed meeting US president Donald Trump in China during talks with Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.
Both US and Russian officials have confirmed in recent days that a possible three-way summit in China was being discussed, but this is the first time Putin has raised the prospect personally.
Any meeting would likely take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China next month, which Trump is already due to attend.
Putin also offered to talkabout restoring economic cooperation between Moscow and Washington, Russian state TV said.
Putin tells Witkoff that Russia is releasing US citizen Stephen Hubbard
Russia has released retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard, who had been imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine, US envoy Steve Witkoff says.
Witkoff is meeting today with Russian president Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg. He says Putin told him that Hubbard was at the St Petersburg airport, Pulkovo, after his release.
Stephen Hubbard, of Michigan, was sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison. Prosecutors said he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian military after Russia sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022, and that he fought alongside them until being captured two months later.
The US government under the Biden administration designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained.
Rubio says Zelensky and Witkoff's meeting was 'positive'
US secretary of state Marco Rubio says special envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky a day earlier had been "positive", with nothing "unexpected" or "surprising".
"He (Witkoff) will now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress," Rubio told reporters in Mumbai today, where he is taking part in a two-day visit to India.
Pictures show a missile crater in Kharkiv after two killed
Pictures have shown the scale of damage in Kharkiv after overnight Russian drone strikes killed two people.
Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram on Wednesday another 11 people suffered stress reactions in the attack that struck private houses and caused other damage.

Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff is facing mounting criticism for describing Russian president Vladimir Putin as a "humanitarian" during their talks in St Petersburg.
Volodymyr Zelensky said a massive Russian aerial attack overnight, which involved at least 21 ballistic missiles and killed two people, showed the US-Russia talks had resulted in "no real change in [Moscow's] attitude".
Without naming Witkoff directly, Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said the Kyiv strikes were "what Russian 'humanism' truly sounds like", adding: "Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war. Only strength will."
There was also growing criticism of Witkoff's remark, which came following Moscow's release of 74-year-old American citizen Stephen Hubbard, back home in Washington. Republican senator Thom Tillis responded with a post on X reading: "WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of 'humanitarian'."
Russian ballistic missiles struck several parts of Kyiv overnight into Thursday, damaging residential buildings, a car service station, a medical facility, a shopping centre and a restaurant. At least 13 explosions were reported in less than eight minutes during one of the three waves of strikes at around 3am local time, according to The Kyiv Independent.
Downing Street hits back at Steve Witkoff over claim Putin is a 'humanitarian'
The UK government has hit back at US special envoy Steve Witkoff's claim that Vladimir Putin is a "humanitarian", saying: "We do not recognise that characterisation."
Speaking to reporters, the prime minister's official spokesperson added: "President Putin has killed thousands of people both innocent Ukrainians and the Russian people who he has sent to their deaths on the front line.
"Ukraine's foreign minister summed it up well this morning when he said that last night the people of Kyiv heard what Russian humanitarianism truly sounds like."
The spokesperson also repeatedly refused to say whether the prime minister thinks President Trump is a humanitarian, instead saying: "We fully support President Trump in his efforts to secure a just and lasting peace in Ukraine."
Russian attack damages shopping centre and residential buildings in Ukraine's Rivne region
German military classifies threat of Russian sabotage as 'significant' for first time - reports
Germany's military has classified the threat of Russian sabotage against its troops and facilities as "significant" for the first time, making it the second-highest threat level, German broadcasters WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported.
This comes after the discovery of a drone carrying explosives near Wunstorf air base in September and reported sabotage incidents involving naval vessels.
"We are noting that we face a significant sabotage threat overall for [Germany's armed forces]," a defence ministry spokesperson said, according to Reuters.
Germany had also accused Moscow of attempting a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August.
The move comes amid growing concerns across Europe about suspected Russian sabotage, cyberattacks and other forms of disruption.
Germany's foreign intelligence chief Martin Jaeger warned earlier this month that the country was in a "shadow war" with Russia and risked being drawn into a violent conflict with Moscow.
Lithuania and Denmark have also reported suspected Russian-linked efforts to target facilities or companies connected to support for Ukraine.
Trump claims Ukraine negotiations are 'closest we've been' to peace
Donald Trump has said negotiations to end the war in Ukraine are "the closest we've been", even as the Kremlin questioned the latest proposals put forward by Kyiv and European leaders.
Trump's comments come as US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg.
Witkoff had discussed the proposals with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky and European leaders in Oslo before travelling to Russia.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Moscow was "in principle, ready to resume" trilateral negotiations in mid-November, but criticised the proposals, saying "there wasn't really much substance in them".
Zelensky has said Ukraine supports restarting the three-way talks as soon as possible.
Witkoff said discussions would continue at a technical level between Washington, Kyiv and Moscow.
Two dead in massive Russian missile attack as Putin talks 'make no difference'
At least two people have died in Russian aerial strikes on Kyiv overnight that involved at least 21 ballistic missiles, Ukrainian officials said.
Three waves of strikes damaged homes and civilian infrastructure including a shopping centre and medical facility, with at least six others reported injured.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attack showed Trump envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg a day earlier had made no difference.
"Almost immediately after another round of talks, Russia launched a pointed attack," Zelensky said.
"This means there has been no real change in its attitude toward everything that is happening.
"It is important to keep trying to find the right solutions to end this war."
Starlink access for Ukraine rests with SpaceX, Rubio says
US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said decisions over Ukraine's access to Starlink satellite communications are a matter for SpaceX and its owner, Elon Musk, rather than the White House.
His remarks followed a Wall Street Journal report that Musk had ordered restrictions on a military-grade version of Starlink used by Ukraine to defend against Russian missile attacks.
Meanwhile, Volodymyr Zelensky earlier said that Washington had resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv on Russian missile strikes following his meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Norway.
The developments come as the United States continues diplomatic engagement with both Ukraine and Russia over a possible end to the war.
'Glaring gaps' leave UK exposed to Russian attacks
Russian authorities claim Ukrainian drone attack on telecom company killed two
Russian authorities in Luhansk said a Ukrainian drone attack on a telecommunications company killed two people.
Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 630 drones had been launched towards the region overnight.
He claimed that the air defences had destroyed most of them, while 163 had been approaching the Russian capital.
Ukrainian foreign minister slams Witkoff's 'appeasement' of Putin
Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha has become the latest figure to hit out at Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff for calling Vladimir Putin a "humanitarian", contrasting the statement with fresh Russian strikes on Kyiv overnight.
Sybiha did not name Witkoff directly, but wrote on X: "Overnight, Kyiv residents heard what Russian 'humanism' truly sounds like: a brutal attack with dozens of ballistic missiles striking energy infrastructure, medical facilities, shopping centres, and residential areas.
"Other cities across Ukraine came under attack as well," he wrote.
"Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war. Only strength will."
